I'm formalizing SimpleGraph.cycleMatroid and have one sorry remaining: the exchange property for forests (acyclic edge sets).

The proof needs: if I and J are acyclic edge sets with |I| < |J|, then ∃ e ∈ J \ I such that I ∪ {e} is still acyclic.

The standard math argument uses the fact that a forest on n vertices with k edges has n - k connected components. I can find IsTree.card_edgeFinset but not the general forest version.

Is this in Mathlib? Or is there a cleaner route to the exchange property?

Everything else compiles (definition, hereditary, compactness): https://github.com/ashanidasgupta1/mathlib-geometry/blob/main/MathlibKG/SimpleGraph/CycleMatroid.lean
I believe you can get what you want from IsAcyclic.card_edgeSet_add_card_connectedComponent in #34910
Thank you @Vlad Tsyrklevich! That's exactly what I needed. I've stubbed the lemma as a sorry'd helper and it type checks. Will replace when #34910 merges.

Could you please make this argument a general constructor for matroids? ie write a function that takes in the data of the independent sets and a proof that all maximal independent sets have the same size and return a term of type Matroid _ _

if it’s of interest i have a development of cycle matroids for general (possibly infinite) simple graphs here — i never cleaned it up for mathlib bc i wasn't sure SimpleGraph was the right generality, but i'm happy to you to take from it as you wish!

I'd like to hear from @Peter Nelson about this, but last I discussed with him about this I think we concluded that multigraphs were the right generality here, and we should wait for that. Or perhaps he or one of his students has it in that generality already.
Ah I didn't know graphic matroids aren't in mathlib already, they were used often in the Seymour project, so I will tag @Martin Dvořák who might have some insights too
Graphic matroids (for multigraphs) are in the matroid repo

The construction relies on a good amount of multigraph stuff that is not yet in mathlib, though @Jun Kwon is working on getting it in.

I think it is quite important that this is done for multigraphs, if it's going into mathlib. From a matroid perspective, insisting that graphs are simple is a nuisance.

Yaël Dillies said:

Could you please make this argument a general constructor for matroids? ie write a function that takes in the data of the independent sets and a proof that all maximal independent sets have the same size and return a term of type Matroid _ _

This isn't possible - there are set systems where the maximal elements are equicardinal, but aren't matroids.
For instance the collection of subsets of {1,2,3,4} that are contained in either {1,2} or {3,4}.
Ah okay, but the argument generalises in some way away from cycle-free sets of vertices, right? What's the correct generalisation?

The definition of Graphic matroid(cycle matroid) requires cycles which, in turn, requires some notion of connectedness and walk. I will advertise that I have a few PRs (#26770, #35905, #35879) that adds properties related to subgraph relation but I was slightly hesitant to make PRs for our definition of walks, in view of discussions happening to have a generalised walk/connectedness definition for all graph-like definitions. As soon as that is resolved, I would be very happy to adapt our code and make a PR towards cycle matroid!

The correct generalization is that for every set X, the maximal independent subsets of X are equicardinal.

This is one of the alternative definitions that you'd see in optimization textbooks. There's no harm in having it as an available constructor, but it isn't something I've needed in years of working with matroids in lean.
